Subject: Final-mile SDK surge mitigation and rollback plan

Hi Eva —

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, here is the working plan for the ‘final-mile’ cutover where TiltPay will migrate live traffic to the Redwood SDK-backed endpoint and we’ll run the surge mitigation and rollback steps if we see abnormal token volumes. Summary below and attached a short playbook (surge_playbook.pdf).

High-level asks
- Confirm cutover window: Target Thu 2026-11-19, 02:00–05:00 PT (we can shift +/- 48h).
- Provide platform contact for an on-call during the window (Samir included on this thread OK?).
- Confirm that Procurement has the signed order in flight (cc'd procurement).

Planned mitigations (short)
- Gradual traffic ramp: 0% → 25% → 50% → 100% over 45 minutes with health checks and p95 latency checks at each step.
- Client-side rate fencing: SDK will honor 429/503 with an exponential backoff (initial 250ms, max 8s, jittered).
- Circuit-breaker: default tripping threshold at 10% error rate sustained for 3m; fallback to a smaller model variant in Redwood routing policy.
- Prefix/KV caching: enable for repeated user prompts to reduce token load during peak.

Why these numbers? Past ramp rehearsals at similar customers showed token cost spikes when bursts exceed 1.8x baseline; the 45m ramp and the 3m error window give a balance between stability and speed-to-recovery.

Attachments: surge_playbook.pdf (runbook), sample_client_snippet.zip (will send in follow-up).

Next steps: If those asks look good I’ll drop a final runbook with exact health-check queries and the SDK snippet (token + timeout guidance).

Thanks,
Jordan

Eva / Samir —

Great — added Samir to the on-call list. Below are the concrete snippets and header guidance you asked for. I’ve also attached sample_client_snippet.zip with a Kotlin + Node example and a short integration test.

1) Timeouts / retries (recommended defaults)
- Mobile clients: connect_timeout=3s, read_timeout=8s, max_retries=3, retry_backoff=exponential(start=250ms, max=3s, jitter=true).
- Backend services: connect_timeout=1.5s, read_timeout=5s, max_retries=5, retry_backoff=exponential(start=150ms, max=8s, jitter=true).
- Rationale: mobile networks have higher tail latencies; longer read_timeout avoids premature client-level cancellations that trigger retries at infra.

2) Rate-limit & telemetry headers we expose (ops-friendly)
- X-Redwood-RateLimit-Limit: tenant quota window size (tokens/sec)
- X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining: tokens left in current window
- X-Redwood-RateLimit-Reset: unix epoch when window resets
- X-Redwood-Request-ID: unique request id for tracing (include in alerts)
- X-Redwood-Model-Variant: model variant served (useful for fallbacks)

Ops rules we recommend you wire in Samir's alerting:
- Trigger auto-escalation when X-Redwood-RateLimit-Remaining < 5% for > 2 minutes across >= 5 hosts.
- Create a synthetic health-check that calls the inference endpoint with a short, deterministic prompt and asserts p95 latency < 450ms.

3) Endpoint migration guidance (cutover checklist highlights)
- Pre-cutover: verify sample_client_snippet passes integration tests against staging with the SDK in 'dry-run' (no traffic shift).
- Cutover: use weighted routing (0→25→50→100) and hold if synthetic health-check fails or error_rate > 3% at a step.
- Post-cutover: keep fallback route to last stable model variant for at least 24h.

4) Surge rollback behavior (what Redwood will do automatically)
- If error rate triggers circuit-breaker, Redwood will route traffic to fallback variant and surface an event to the team (X-Redwood-Event: circuit_breaker_tripped).
- We will also mark the route as degraded in the Console and open an internal incident if p95 latency > 1200ms for > 5 minutes.

HubSpot deal and runbook link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/4721 (internal) — I added the playbook under the drive link in the metadata.

Let me know any tweaks; I can fold them into the final PDF and the DocuSign order if procurement needs an updated SOW.
